skill.name: browser-extension-developer
skill.description: Develop and maintain WXT browser extensions in the browser directory, including Chrome, Firefox, Edge, content scripts, background scripts, and i18n updates.
skill.summary: Guides cross-browser WXT extension development, builds, compatibility checks, and localization updates.
skill.author: yamadashy

content.value_statement: Cross-browser extension work often breaks across Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and localization files. This skill guides WXT extension development, builds, compatibility checks, and i18n updates.
actual_capabilities: Guide development inside the browser directory for a WXT extension.
Support Chrome, Firefox, and Edge compatibility decisions.
Identify content script and background script areas from the documented structure.
Use documented npm commands for development, build, lint, and test workflows.
Guide locale file additions for the listed twelve languages.
Account for Chrome API usage and Firefox polyfill needs.
limitations: It only documents the browser extension area of the repository.
It assumes the project uses the documented WXT structure.
It does not guarantee browser store approval or policy compliance.
It does not replace manual testing in each target browser.

use_cases.title: Add Extension Features
use_cases.description: Plan and implement a browser extension change across content scripts and background scripts.

use_cases.title: Verify Browser Compatibility
use_cases.description: Check whether a change needs Chrome API handling, Firefox polyfills, or Edge-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Expand Localization
use_cases.description: Add or update locale messages for supported extension languages.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Extension Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the browser extension structure and explain where content script, background script, config, and locale changes should go.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Add this browser extension behavior while keeping Chrome, Firefox, and Edge compatibility in mind: [describe behavior].

prompt_templates.title: Add a Locale
prompt_templates.prompt: Add or update extension localization for [language code]. Include the required message keys and check existing language patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Cross-Browser Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the extension changes for WXT build readiness, browser compatibility risks, lint coverage, tests, and localization completeness.

output_examples.input: Review a new content script change for cross-browser risk.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering API compatibility, injected button behavior, Firefox polyfill needs, and recommended validation steps.

output_examples.input: Add a new supported language for extension messages.
output_examples.output: A localization checklist with required message names, existing language references, and validation steps for translated extension text.

output_examples.input: Prepare the extension for a release build.
output_examples.output: A release readiness summary covering development commands, build targets, lint checks, tests, and manual browser verification.

best_practices: Run lint and tests before marking extension work complete.
Test changes in each target browser before release.
Keep locale message keys aligned across all supported languages.
anti_patterns: Assuming Chrome APIs work unchanged in Firefox.
Changing content scripts without validating GitHub page behavior.
Adding locale files with missing required message keys.

faq.question: Which browsers does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Chrome, Firefox, and Edge browser extension development.

faq.question: Which framework does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes the extension uses the WXT framework.

faq.question: Can it help with content scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for content script and background script work.

faq.question: Can it help with localization?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes supported languages and required message keys.

faq.question: Does it publish extensions to browser stores?
faq.answer: No. It helps with development and validation, not store submission.

faq.question: Does it run npm commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands for the developer to run when appropriate.
